hints.title: Binary Exponentiation Halving Strategy
hints.text: Multiplying x repeatedly by itself n times takes linear time. How can squaring the base halve the exponent at each step?

hints.title: Parity Exponent Reduction Invariant
hints.text: When exponent n is even, x raised to n equals x squared raised to n / 2. When n is odd, multiply the accumulator by current base.

hints.title: Iterative Base Squaring Procedure
hints.text: Handle negative exponent by inverting x and negating n. Iterate while exponent is positive: if the exponent is odd, multiply answer by current base; square current base and integer divide exponent by two. Return answer.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Multiplying n times linearly takes O(N) operations, which fails when n reaches 2^31 - 1.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Repeated squaring computes the result in O(log N) iterations with O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate must handle edge cases including n = 0, negative n, and 32-bit integer overflow when negating -2^31.
